newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX takes tumble in post-bourse dealings.
newsitem.headline: German DAX takes tumble in post-bourse dealings.

text.p: The German share market see-sawed on Tuesday, first stuttering after a Wall Street-led surge, then regaining poise to send the blue chip DAX index to its second consecutive record closing high in bourse trade.
The 30-share DAX ended the bourse session up 19.78 points, or 0.55 percent, at 3,595.15 points, and looked poised to continue its bull run, many dealers said.
But the DAX took a tumble in post-bourse IBIS electronic dealings, falling 33.85 points to 3,559.29 points on a hefty bout of profit-taking and a lack of interest in the market.
Volumes were modest apart from selected big-ticket stocks, and bemoaned what they said was relatively low activity from investors, even after more overnight records on Wall Street.
"We see no broad-based buy interest," said a dealer.

The DAX did not manage to sustain a push that sent the IBIS DAX index, which tracks all-day electronic trade in blue chips, to within a hair's breadth of an all-time intraday high of 3,612.46 points in the first hour of pre-bourse dealings.

One of the pressures on trade was a slide by Deutsche Telekom AG, partly correcting a recent surge, after the telecommunications giant released 1996 data which partly exceeded bullish forecasts, but did not surprise, dealers said.

The company posted group net profit of 1.8 billion marks for the year, but eased 1.06 marks, or 2.4 percent, to 40.13 marks, after notching up gains of as much as five percent at its height on Monday.

The other heavy focus of the day was Deutsche Bank AG, which closed up 2.20 marks at 97.30 marks, just off an all-time high of 97.75 marks. Dealers attributed its gains to technical factors, partly connected to an options expiry deadline on Friday.
